aristotle-metaphysics-ross-q001.title: q001 — Multiple senses ordered to a primary reference
aristotle-metaphysics-ross-q001.provenance: selected W. D. Ross online translation read; paraphrase-ready, no print or Greek collation and no exact quotation claim.
aristotle-metaphysics-ross-q001.content:
**Paraphrase:** Healthy uses refer differently to health through preservation, production, indication or receptivity; medical uses likewise relate to an art. Aristotle coordinates different senses of being through a primary reference and identifies substance as the primary object of the inquiry. The differentiated relations belong to one investigation without having an identical definition or function.

**Locator:** IV.2, opening argument; project locator 1003a33–1003b19.

aristotle-nicomachean-ethics-ross-q002.title: q002 — Exchange, demand and conventional money
aristotle-nicomachean-ethics-ross-q002.provenance: selected W. D. Ross online translation read; paraphrase-ready, no print or Greek collation and no exact quotation claim.
aristotle-nicomachean-ethics-ross-q002.content:
**Paraphrase:** The builder and shoemaker bring unlike products into proportion for reciprocal exchange. Money represents demand by convention; users can alter it or render it useless. Aristotle qualifies commensurability: goods so different are not strictly commensurable, but become sufficiently comparable relative to demand. This is his philosophical treatment, not independently verified coinage history.

**Locator:** V.5.

**Verification:** selected W. D. Ross online translation read; paraphrase-ready, no print or Greek collation and no exact quotation claim.

aristotle-politics-jowett-q002.title: q002 — Provision, use and accumulation
aristotle-politics-jowett-q002.provenance: selected Benjamin Jowett online translation read; paraphrase-ready, no print or Greek collation and no exact quotation claim.
aristotle-politics-jowett-q002.content:
**Paraphrase:** Acquisition provides what household management uses. A shoe can serve wear or exchange; coined money facilitates exchange, and accumulation can become a separate unlimited end. Aristotle distinguishes this end from bounded provision and censures usury. These are his evaluative distinctions and origin narrative. The text’s endorsement of hierarchy and coercive acquisition remains part of its historical position.

**Locator:** I.8–10.

taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy-ct12.content: > **#1 — `Ø`, the occlusion mark.** The slash is *fused into the zero*, indistinguishable from the apparent self, so Ø appears as a **singular thing, the bound self** rather than as a composite sign. The Cartesian *cogito* is the philosophical canonisation of this fusion — the slash treated as *the I*, the zero behind it covered over. Hume finds only the impressions the slash produced and calls the zero empty. **Descartes and Hume sit at the same position** (#1), differing only over which side of Ø they fixate on; both miss that **Ø is the occlusion mark.** Western modernity sits at chronic #1-fixation. - **Locator:** §IX, line 481. **Provenance:** `working/sources-texts-references/10-7-2026-core-theorems-pithy.md`. taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy-ct13.title: CT-13 — §IX, the set-theoretic floor (line 494)
taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy-ct13.provenance: working/sources-texts-references/10-7-2026-core-theorems-pithy.md`. Authorial native QL text at the existing locator; internal derivation, not external corroboration.
taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy-ct13.content: > **Set-theoretic floor (Draft 3).** Set theory already writes the two our way. In von Neumann's construction the ordinal `2` *is* the set `{0, 1}` — two as the *holding-together* of zero and one, each number born as the collection of its predecessors, the successor an act of **emission from the void upward**: `∅`, then `{∅}`, then `{∅, {∅}}`. So `1 = {∅} = {0}` — **the singleton that holds the void**, the mark whose entire content is its binding of the ground. The `1` is not a second thing beside the `0`; it is *the void gathered into a set*, the linker that makes the ground countable as one. `2 = 0/1` is the standard notation "read with the reverence it never asked for"; against it the fallen `1 + (−1)` is a late arrival (debt-bookkeeping). - **Locator:** §IX, line 494. **Provenance:** `working/sources-texts-references/10-7-2026-core-theorems-pithy.md`. taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy-ct14.title: CT-14 — §IX, the Lacan bridge: S1 against anusyūta (lines 496–498)
taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy-ct14.provenance: working/sources-texts-references/10-7-2026-core-theorems-pithy.md`. Authorial native QL text at the existing locator; internal derivation, not external corroboration.
taylor-2026-core-theorems-pithy-ct14.content: > **Lacanian bridge (Immutable Subject).** In the symbolic register the linking `1` is the **master signifier `S1`** — the *point de capiton*, the quilting button that retroactively arrests the sliding chain and constitutes it as having-said-something by quilting the other signifiers (`S2`) under itself. Lacan left this *wholly contingent* — the button arbitrary, the symbolic without anchor. What he was reaching for is the [[working/sources-texts-references/QL-Essay-Rewrite#1.3 The Emergence of Spanda|Spanda]] **`anusyūta`**: the *stitched-through-ness*, the **pre-quilting thread** beneath all cognitions (*I am happy, I am pained…*) without which no quilting could button anything, because the chain would not hold as a chain. *Anusyūta is not a quilting point — it is the thread.* > The matheme places it: **the kartṛ-pole is the anusyūta-thread** (Layer 1, the un-objectifiable that any signifying activity presupposes). *The slide is real because the threader doesn't slide.* The signifying chain is kārya (perishable, articulated, oscillating in vikalpa-mode); the threader is kartṛ (structurally not the kind of thing that can be a signifier). **Lacan had the topology of the local cut without the ontology of the global thread; the matheme supplies the thread without falsifying the cut.** - **Locator:** §IX, lines 496 and 498. **Provenance:** `working/sources-texts-references/10-7-2026-core-theorems-pithy.md`. > We are impelled, then, to return to the cogito and slow it down. Descartes hears the indubitable correctly: in thinking, doubting, or being deceived, there is presence. Yet "I think, therefore I am" lets the I be gathered too quickly into the act of thinking, as though the user of the instrument could be secured by the instrument's operation. The sentence has to open: I am aware of thinking. Thought is the means of knowing, the determinate activity through which something is grasped. Awareness is the fact in which that activity appears.
